title: Artificial intelligence as a cultural tool: Heuristic potentials and limitations of the metaphor
abstract: Context and relevance. The large-scale adoption of artificial intelligence systems in education, professional activity, and everyday life challenges established psychological conceptions of development, mediation, and subjectivity. Within cultural-historical psychology, AI is most often analyzed through the metaphor of a cultural tool, which appears to preserve theoretical continuity but may obscure the fundamentally novel nature of digital sociotechnical systems. Objective. Through theoretical analysis, to identify the advantages and disadvantages of considering artificial intelligence as a cultural tool within the logic of cultural-historical psychology. Hypothesis. The cultural tool metaphor has significant heuristic potential for analyzing the mediation of activity involving AI; however, its explanatory capabilities are limited and, when applied uncritically, lead to conceptual reductions. Theoretical framework. The study is based on a reconstruction of key tenets of the cultural-historical and activity traditions, as well as on interdisciplinary work in the philosophy of technology, the anthropology of digital technologies, and critical AI studies. Results. It is shown that AI radically breaks the link between the mediation of activity and the mediation of development, redistributes agency and responsibility, and also generates effects of reverse mediation, influencing the subject's way of thinking and self-evaluation. It is revealed that the language of the cultural tool carries a latent normative effect, contributing to the naturalization of technological change. Conclusions. Artificial intelligence represents the first mass cultural means introduced without a cultural-psychological project of subject development. This positions AI not merely as an object of analysis but as a challenge to cultural-historical psychology itself, necessitating a reconsideration of key concepts.
